regions.merged_text: positively nothing less than blasphemous in the "Great Press" of to-day, because "Bitterly hostile to justice and truth" and therefore hostile to God himself who is eternally both. (See encyc'1 Leo XIII-1902) A civilized humanity, or as uncivilized, we act in general these days as though that power were nothing more than a childish myth. How? We sacrifice untold millions of our choicest youth and manhood for the prin- ciple of "Self-Determination" - nothing more or less in reality than a jus- tification of the Catholic Dogma of "Free Will" - and the nations stand mute at the 74 days martyrdom of a MacSweeney protesting and the age-long cru- cifixion of his nation protesting in the name of that same awful sacrifice and in the name of eternal justice against nothing less that the astounding outrage of an international attempt to destroy that very fundamental prin- ciple" - that God-given faculty. Does not such silence alone brand our so-called civilization as a sham and a farce? An outrage it is, pure and simple, on intelligence and decency. Does it not brand the professions of the allied nations for their war against and their degradation of Central Europe as manifest hypocrisy? Let no nation, much less individuals deceive themselves: God will not be mocked forever! And the allied nations, and their civilzation have been mocking the honest peoples of the earth, and surely not less the Eternal God of honest people. Who is to blame? Where is our ideal Catholic Press? Offensive and Defensive? God help us! Aye, God help us, and forgive us! That individual leaders have been and are guilty of that criminal silence and that mockery, is as positively clear as the fact that nations are made up of individuals. They seem now, however, to be going further into crime. In- stead of blushing for shame, personal as well as national, that no one has a- risen like Daniel of old to convict the hypocrites, some of them are be- ginning to come out on the side of shame itself, on the side of the bull-dog and the lion -- the side of the arch-ravager of nations. They speculate with the coolness of game-cook gamblers on hair-splitting points of morality, thus wittingly or unwittingly-diverting attention from the real source of troubles in Ireland-the presence of British Soldiers, and of British corrup- tion (See Dr. Ryan, E.G. in"America" ) Is not this clearly a case of the Scriptural, "Straining at a gnat, and swallowing a camel?" Shame on the "blind Guides"! Pardon me if your correspondent seem acrimonious, and may the Lord help us to see clearly! for Bittemess like falsity and Exaggeration is to no purpose in an honest cause. But history, it seems here as well as elsewhere, must repeat itself, It was a Bishop that condemned St. Joan of Arc for witchery and that a little later, durressed as he was by the British (and at that, time supposed to be a Catholic), exposed her to unmentionable cruelties and finally burned her at the stake as a heretic. If reports be true there are one or two pre- lates in America who would do the like for a number of Irish Joans, even without British duress.
